root_cause.text: The control message buffer was allocated with devm_kzalloc tied to the parent USB device (udev->dev) instead of the USB interface device (intf->dev), causing the buffer's lifetime to outlive the driver unbind and result in a memory leak when the driver is unbound without physical disconnection.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `devm_kzalloc(&udev->dev, ...)` to `devm_kzalloc(&intf->dev, ...)`, and the commit description explicitly states that "USB drivers bind to USB interfaces and any device managed resources should have their lifetime tied to the interface rather than parent USB device" and that the fix ensures "the control message buffer lifetime so that it is released on driver unbind."

intent_record.how: This ensures the allocated memory is associated with the USB interface device instead of the USB device, so that the memory is automatically freed when the interface is released rather than when the USB device is removed.
